rankings_ref: .agent_workspace/round1/rankings.json (2026-07 DataEye-ADX x 引力引擎联合月榜, both charts)

mechanic_score.question: Can the core gameplay loop (one complete session) be replicated in vanilla JS/HTML5 (Canvas2D/WebGL/WebAudio/WASM, no engine, no wx.*, no server)?

product_score.question: Can full commercial product parity (monetization, acquisition, social fabric, liveops, compliance) be achieved off-platform by a competent independent studio that is not the original IP holder?

scale: 1-10 on both axes; 10 = easiest/fullest replication. Absolute scale: no game reaches high P because the WeChat platform fabric (chat-graph distribution, ad economics, one-tap payment, compliance absorption) has no generic equivalent (Round 1 gaps G1-G12).
rounding: score = weighted sum rounded half-up; documented judgment adjustment of at most +/-1 allowed and recorded in the 'adjustment' field
vanilla_js_policy: Browser-standard APIs only, no game engine. OSS WASM libs (e.g. Rapier) allowed with an M3 deduction; engine_assisted_mechanic_score shows the score with an OSS engine stack for comparability with Round 1.

mechanic.rationale: Merge-TD campaign session runs fully offline; text-as-units renders trivially with canvas fillText (radically cheap art). Deductions: 1v1 online PvP is a headline mode (needs netcode or bots) and the CJK word/character content plus wave balance must exist before the loop is testable.

product.rationale: Hybrid IAA+IAP is partially portable natively, but matchmaking liquidity requires platform-scale DAU, the season ladder needs a backend, and the Chinese-character mechanic is culture-bound (does not localize), capping the global path.

mechanic.rationale: Fully offline deterministic tile-DAG; proven on this branch: prototypes/sheep-match3 and prototypes/tile-trio implement the loop with solvability generation and headless verification in plain JS. Daily level can be locally seeded.

product.rationale: The product is a CN-chat social phenomenon: difficulty-cliff brag/share loop (P2=1), province/friend rank boards, rewarded-ad revives on 流量主 economics. Backend is light (level-of-day service + pass-rate telemetry) but that cannot rescue parity; its specific rage-share formula did not transfer in global clones.

mechanic.rationale: Pure algorithmic unblock/rush-hour puzzle: grid logic plus tween animation, fully offline. Levels are solver-generatable with minimum-move validation, so even content bootstrap is cheap.

product.rationale: Best P in the corpus: light social coupling, minimal backend, procedurally sustainable content, and a proven global genre (unblock puzzles) with original IP. Ceiling remains the missing CN-web rewarded-video economy and platform discovery.

mechanic.rationale: Loop is fully offline, but a 3D rigid-body pile of hundreds of items with raycast picking is impractical in hand-authored vanilla JS: raw-WebGL scene management (M2=5) and 3D physics (M3=4) gate it. With Three.js + Rapier WASM (all OSS) it scores 8, matching Round 1. The corpus's only client-tech moat.

product.rationale: IAA economics and share loops are the dependencies; backend is light (async ranks, ad-gated tools). Global genre analogs exist, so an off-platform product is plausible at lower eCPM.

mechanic.rationale: Tap-to-find with hit regions and zoom/pan is trivial canvas work; the only real cost is that the loop's content IS authored art scenes (hundreds needed), hence M4=3.

product.rationale: Hidden-object is a proven global genre; parity is gated by a permanent original-art production pipeline (scene cadence) and rewarded-ad hint economics rather than by any platform API.

mechanic.rationale: Falling-sand cellular automata on Canvas 2D with typed arrays is classic vanilla-JS territory; color-sort win detection is simple, and levels are largely procedural.

product.rationale: Standard IAA sort-puzzle economics: light backend, sustainable content, global genre analogs (sand/water sort); the CN-web ad-economy gap is the ceiling.

mechanic.rationale: Rendering and defense logic are easy 2D work, but the asymmetric raid/defense against other players' layouts is central to the loop; a solo slice with bot layouts is replicable, full loop needs rooms/netcode.

product.rationale: Needs player liquidity for the asymmetric loop plus rooms/matchmaking/anti-cheat backend; growth rode CN short-video/chat distribution that does not transfer.

mechanic.rationale: Same family as 挪了下车: grid move/sort logic, fully offline, solver-generatable levels; slightly richer piece semantics than pure unblock.

product.rationale: Same profile as 挪了下车 with a weaker brand: minimal backend, procedural content, global sort-puzzle genre; capped by ad economics and discovery.

mechanic.rationale: Sort-elimination with simple agent pathing (ants carrying items) — deterministic queueing logic plus light animation, all comfortably vanilla canvas.

product.rationale: Standard IAA sort-casual profile: light backend, sustainable content, global analogs; CN-web ad-economy gap is the ceiling.

mechanic.rationale: 2.5D layered plates with constraint checks (which screws are free) and light fake physics for falling plates; authored levels need solvability validation, all within vanilla JS.

product.rationale: Screw-puzzle genre has proven global analogs; parity gated by ad economics and level-content cadence, not platform APIs.

games.genre: Roguelike割草射击 + 塔防 + 轻RPG养成

mechanic.rationale: A single wave-defense run with three-choice roguelike upgrades is fully offline and deterministic (seeded). Cost is performance engineering: hundreds of projectiles/entities with dense VFX on canvas requires pooling and careful batching; ballistics/knockback are fake-physics.

product.rationale: Best monetization parity on the grossing chart — its own developer proved the native-app path with hybrid IAA+IAP. The moat is deep meta (gear/talents/seasons/guilds), liveops cadence, and a WeChat-ads UA machine; CN standalone needs 版号.

games.genre: 冰雪生存模拟经营 + 三国4X SLG

mechanic.rationale: Client math is easy (timers, resource economy), but the retention loop — alliance war on a persistent world shard — cannot exist client-side; only a single-player city-builder slice is vanilla-JS replicable. Large 2.5D city/world-map scenes without an engine add friction.

product.rationale: Parity requires a sharded persistent world, alliance realtime ops, anti-cheat, and a liveops organization plus SLG-scale paid UA — an engineering program, not a project. Alliance social fabric needs player critical mass a clone will not have.

games.genre: 国风修仙放置RPG + 开箱装备养成

mechanic.rationale: Kill-loot-equip idle loop with auto-battle is straightforward client logic; spine-style 2D RPG presentation is real but tractable canvas work. Class/beast/gear tables and balance must exist before the loop is meaningful.

product.rationale: Server-authoritative economy, PvP, deep content cadence, and IAP rails with 版号 for CN standalone; the xianxia theme is CN-market-bound.

games.genre: 海上生存模拟经营 + 卡牌养成 + 轻SLG

mechanic.rationale: The scavenge/production-chain/base loop is offline-able, but the game couples three systems (economy sim, card collection, alliance city wars) and only the first is self-contained; content volume is large before the loop resembles the product.

product.rationale: Three coupled systems each need server authority; alliance city wars add SLG-class backend and player-mass requirements on top of sim liveops.

games.genre: 种花/插花模拟经营 + 社交

mechanic.rationale: Plant/harvest/order/decorate loop is simple client logic and fully offline-able; the cost is the large decoration asset base, which is content production rather than mechanics.

product.rationale: Casual-sim IAP conversion is proven globally in the genre; parity is gated by permanent content/liveops cadence, server-driven economy and events, and social visits — production burden, not platform APIs.

games.genre: 开箱养成 + 休闲RPG/闯关

mechanic.rationale: Loot-box opening, gear comparison, and stage-push action levels are replicable client-side; action feel (input latency, animation polish) is the main vanilla-JS effort.

product.rationale: Loot economy needs server authority; cross-server PvP, seasonal liveops, and IAP-scale UA make off-platform parity a sustained operation.

games.genre: 中式微恐RPG + 轻量搜打撤 + 放置养成

mechanic.rationale: Single-map search, auto-battle, extraction, and meta upgrades are mechanically moderate; the horror atmosphere (lighting, audio, art direction) is where the real cost sits, and the loop needs substantial content before it feels like the product.

product.rationale: Hero meta and events need server ops; the product's pull is content/atmosphere volume with CN-culture theming that does not transfer, plus 版号 for CN standalone.

games.genre: 冰雪生存模拟经营 + 4X SLG

mechanic.rationale: A furnace/city-builder slice is vanilla-JS replicable, but the core loop is a persistent 4X world with alliances — inherently server-side. It is a native-app port (Whiteout Survival), so the client is engine-built with content scale far beyond a vanilla scope.

product.rationale: Off-platform viability is proven by the original itself (the native app), but for a replicator parity means building a Whiteout-class SLG backend, anti-cheat, and a liveops org, then buying SLG-CAC traffic — the largest program in the corpus.

games.genre: 随机英雄合成 + Roguelike塔防

mechanic.rationale: Three-minute summon/merge/hold-the-line runs with seeded randomness are an excellent vanilla-JS fit; moderate entity density needs pooling but no physics.

product.rationale: Hero pool, balance matrix, co-op/PvP modes and hybrid monetization require ongoing server ops and content cadence; genre has global analogs so the ceiling is operational, not structural.

games.genre: 二合（merge-2）+ 田园建造/模拟经营

mechanic.rationale: Merge-2 board, task chains, and scene restoration are classic, fully offline client mechanics — among the easiest on the grossing chart.

product.rationale: Adjusted -1: the product is built on the 芒果TV variety-show license (IP, cast likenesses, show content) that a replicator cannot obtain — parity is structurally unattainable, not merely hard. Generic merge-farm parity is a different product.

games.chart_basis: 2017 launch icon; evergreen casual staple (Round 1 blended top-10 member)

mechanic.rationale: Hold-to-charge ballistic hop with landing check and procedural platforms; a working vanilla-canvas replica already exists on this branch (prototypes/jump-jump). The mechanically easiest title in the corpus.

product.rationale: Adjusted -1: the formula lets a trivial backend (P4=8) rescue a product whose entire value — friend/group leaderboards inside chat and zero-friction launch — was rated blocking (G2/G3) in Round 1. Without an ambient social graph the clone is a hollow tech demo; monetization was never the point.

games.chart_basis: 畅销榜 #28 (2026-07); era-defining 2023-24 #1 (Round 1 blended top-10 member)

mechanic.rationale: The idle chop-chop loop (auto-battle, loot, upgrade timers) is easy vanilla JS; spine-style presentation is moderate work. The hard part — economy design and balance tables — is content, not code.

product.rationale: Its success formula was WeChat-ad-network UA arbitrage plus IAP rails, server-authoritative economy, cross-server async PvP, and rapid liveops iteration — none of which transfers off-platform.
